result:
I've written experiment 23's design to `runs/pending_experiment.json`. It's a valid JSON file, and the only file I touched.

**Where things stand.** The current best is experiment 20 at 0.078. On the held-out 2024 photograph it gives 93.0% usable fixes, 0.75% false fixes (3 frames) and 6.25% abstentions (25 frames). The three training photographs score 100% usable at the same viewpoints, so what's left is the gap between photographs, and most of it is abstention. Two other recent results:
- **Experiment 21 (train the head first on a frozen trunk) was never tested.** Its training log ends in an AWS connection error (`EndpointConnectionError`, could not reach the EC2 endpoint) after its fourth epoch, so the 1e9 score says nothing about the idea. Up to that point its numbers tracked experiment 20 almost exactly, so I didn't re-run it.
- **Experiment 22 (randomly shifting each training view by up to ±12 px) was worse,** at 0.103.

**The design: "Same place, same belief"** (a training-only loss change).
- **The problem it targets:** the training log's own check shows that each committee member names the same tile for a place across the three training photographs only 84% of the time on clean views. Nothing in the loss asks it to. Also, although each data chunk holds every place in all three photographs, each 64-view batch is a random draw from the chunk. So the three views of one place almost never reach the same training step.
- **Change 1:** each batch becomes 21 places × all 3 photographs (63 views). The batch-norm recalibration pass uses the same grouping.
- **Change 2:** each member gets a penalty (Jensen-Shannon divergence, weight 6) when its tile-belief maps for one place differ across the three photographs, either in where they point or in how sure they are. This follows AugMix (Hendrycks et al., ICLR 2020). The members stay independent of each other.
- **Why it's new:** earlier attempts to make a place look the same across photographs (experiments 3, 8 and 9) acted on internal features, before the pretrained trunk existed. Experiment 9 crashed without a score. This one acts on the belief map, which is what the confidence gate actually reads.
- **Prediction:** mission score about 0.05–0.07, with usable fixes at 94–95.5% and false fixes at or below 0.75%.
- **How to read it:** the per-photograph agreement figure in the log should rise above 0.9. If it rises and the 2024 score doesn't move, then agreement among three photographs doesn't carry over to a fourth. If agreement doesn't rise, the idea wasn't really tested at this weight.

Graph, export, model size (31.7 MB) and latency stay exactly as in experiment 20.

The implementation brief restates the CLI and ONNX contracts and the rule that nothing may open the 2024 photograph. It also has the code check that the grouped batching is laid out correctly.
